Hello,

I am running a model of plant/microbe data and am getting the error " lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified"

The model has: 
high degrees of freedom
Experimental treatments: w, t
Environmental variables (temp, moisture N)
Response variables: PlantBiom, Plant Richness, Phyla Richness

The model does not have:
latent variables... could this be the problem...or is it okay to run strictly as a path analysis?

Here is the code

mod3 <- '
soil_temp_ave ~ t + PlantBiom + soil_moisture_ave
soil_moisture_ave ~ w+t+soil_temp_ave + PlantBiom
TOTAL_N ~ soil_moisture_ave + PlantBiom + soil_temp_ave + PlantBiom
ph ~ soil_moisture_ave
PlantBiom ~ soil_temp_ave + soil_moisture_ave + TOTAL_N + ph + PhylaRich + PlantRichness
PlantRichness ~ soil_moisture_ave + TOTAL_N + PlantBiom
PhylaRich ~  soil_moisture_ave + TOTAL_N + ph + PlantBiom
'

mod3fit <- sem(mod3,julyphylumdat.h2oxotc.noNA)
summary(mod3fit, standardized=TRUE,fit.measures=TRUE)

Here is the output from R:
-  I understand warning message 1 and know that it is bc biomass has a larger variance than anything else, but I don't think this is leading to the problems as I have used biomass in other SEM models that have worked...

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified
parts:
You have a complex nonrecursive structuralmodel,with many reciprocal relationships.  When A predicts B and B predicts A, you usually need at least one of the two to have its own predictor, unshared with the other in the pair.  But you don't just have pairs--you have tangles of reciprocal relations.  You will need to learn about the rank and order conditions for identification of structural models.  Bollen (1989) in his classic Structural Equations with Latent Variables, actually presents a very readable treatment.
     Lots of DF does not protect you from identification problems.  Nonnegative DF is a necessary but not sufficient condition for identification.
     I agree with you that Warning 1 is not the central cause of your problem. However, strange numbers can result from that "outlier variance" condition.  I would suggest rescaling--say, dividing that variable by 10 or by 100--to take that issue off the table, too.
